       SUM(oi.quantity * oi.unit_price) AS revenue,
       COUNT(*)                         AS line_count
FROM   order_items oi
JOIN   orders   o ON o.order_id    = oi.order_id
JOIN   products p ON p.product_id  = oi.product_id
WHERE  o.status = 'COMPLETED'

-- ============================================================================
-- solution.sql — Schema + Bulk Load + Optimize
--
-- Run with:   psql -v ON_ERROR_STOP=1 -f solution.sql
--
-- 1. DDL for customers / products / orders / order_items (exactly as schema.sql)
-- 2. Set-based bulk load (deterministic, seeded):
--      customers   10,000
--      products     1,000
--      orders     100,000   status COMPLETED ~50%, PENDING/CANCELLED/REFUNDED
--                           ~1/6 each; order_date uniform over
--                           2025-06-01 .. 2026-09-30
--      order_items ~300,000 (1..5 lines per order); orders.total_amount is
--                           the exact sum of its lines
--    Indexes are built AFTER the load (much faster than maintaining them
--    row-by-row during the insert).
-- 3. Indexes for target_query.sql, then VACUUM ANALYZE.
-- ============================================================================

\set ON_ERROR_STOP on
SET client_min_messages = warning;

-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- 1. DDL (verbatim from schema.sql)
-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
DROP TABLE IF EXISTS order_items CASCADE;
DROP TABLE IF EXISTS orders CASCADE;
DROP TABLE IF EXISTS products CASCADE;
DROP TABLE IF EXISTS customers CASCADE;

CREATE TABLE customers (
    customer_id   bigint PRIMARY KEY,
    customer_name varchar(120) NOT NULL,
    email         varchar(200) NOT NULL,
    country       varchar(2)   NOT NULL,
    created_at    timestamptz  NOT NULL DEFAULT now()
);

CREATE TABLE products (
    product_id   bigint PRIMARY KEY,
    product_name varchar(160) NOT NULL,
    category     varchar(60)  NOT NULL,
    unit_price   numeric(10,2) NOT NULL
);

CREATE TABLE orders (
    order_id     bigint PRIMARY KEY,
    customer_id  bigint NOT NULL REFERENCES customers(customer_id),
    order_date   timestamptz NOT NULL,
    status       varchar(20) NOT NULL,
    total_amount numeric(12,2) NOT NULL
);

CREATE TABLE order_items (
    order_item_id bigint PRIMARY KEY,
    order_id      bigint NOT NULL REFERENCES orders(order_id),
    product_id    bigint NOT NULL REFERENCES products(product_id),
    quantity      integer NOT NULL,
    unit_price    numeric(10,2) NOT NULL
);

-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- 2. Bulk load — one transaction, set-based INSERT ... SELECT generate_series
-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
BEGIN;

SELECT setseed(0.42);   -- reproducible dataset

-- customers: 10k
INSERT INTO customers (customer_id, customer_name, email, country, created_at)
SELECT g,
       'Customer ' || g,
       'customer' || g || '@example.com',
       (ARRAY['US','GB','DE','FR','ES','IT','NL','SE','JP','BR','CA','AU'])
           [1 + floor(random() * 12)::int],
       TIMESTAMPTZ '2024-01-01' + random() * INTERVAL '500 days'
FROM generate_series(1, 10000) AS g;

-- products: 1k across 10 categories
INSERT INTO products (product_id, product_name, category, unit_price)
SELECT g,
       'Product ' || g,
       (ARRAY['Electronics','Books','Clothing','Home','Garden','Toys',
              'Sports','Beauty','Grocery','Automotive'])[1 + (g % 10)],
       round((2 + random() * 498)::numeric, 2)
FROM generate_series(1, 1000) AS g;

-- Order headers staged first so total_amount can be computed from the lines
-- before the orders rows are written (no post-load UPDATE / dead tuples).
CREATE TEMP TABLE stage_orders ON COMMIT DROP AS
SELECT g                                               AS order_id,
       1 + floor(random() * 10000)::bigint             AS customer_id,
       -- uniform over 2025-06-01 00:00 .. 2026-09-30 23:59:59
       TIMESTAMPTZ '2025-06-01'
         + random() * (TIMESTAMPTZ '2026-10-01' - TIMESTAMPTZ '2025-06-01')
                                                       AS order_date,
       CASE WHEN r < 0.50 THEN 'COMPLETED'
            WHEN r < 0.70 THEN 'PENDING'
            WHEN r < 0.85 THEN 'CANCELLED'
            ELSE               'REFUNDED'
       END                                             AS status,
       1 + floor(random() * 5)::int                    AS n_lines
FROM (SELECT g, random() AS r FROM generate_series(1, 100000) AS g) s;

CREATE TEMP TABLE stage_items ON COMMIT DROP AS
SELECT row_number() OVER (ORDER BY so.order_id, l.line) AS order_item_id,
       so.order_id,
       l.product_id,
       l.quantity,
       p.unit_price
FROM   stage_orders so
CROSS  JOIN LATERAL (
         SELECT line,
                1 + floor(random() * 1000)::bigint AS product_id,
                1 + floor(random() * 10)::int      AS quantity
         FROM   generate_series(1, so.n_lines) AS line
       ) l
JOIN   products p ON p.product_id = l.product_id;

INSERT INTO orders (order_id, customer_id, order_date, status, total_amount)
SELECT so.order_id, so.customer_id, so.order_date, so.status,
       COALESCE(t.total, 0)
FROM   stage_orders so
LEFT   JOIN (SELECT order_id, SUM(quantity * unit_price) AS total
             FROM stage_items GROUP BY order_id) t USING (order_id)
ORDER  BY so.order_id;

INSERT INTO order_items (order_item_id, order_id, product_id, quantity, unit_price)
SELECT order_item_id, order_id, product_id, quantity, unit_price
FROM   stage_items
ORDER  BY order_item_id;

COMMIT;

-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- 3. Indexes
-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- The target query filters  status = 'COMPLETED' AND order_date >= '2026-01-01'
-- which matches ~28% of orders (50% COMPLETED x ~9/16 months). At that
-- selectivity a plain (status, order_date) index that has to visit the heap
-- loses to a seq scan, so the index is made COVERING (INCLUDE order_id, the
-- only other orders column the query reads). With an all-visible heap
-- (VACUUM below) the planner serves orders from an Index Only Scan:
-- equality column first, range column second, join key as payload.
CREATE INDEX orders_status_order_date_idx
    ON orders (status, order_date) INCLUDE (order_id);

-- FK-side index on order_items.order_id: supports the orders -> order_items
-- join (and FK checks / deletes on orders). product_id likewise for products.
CREATE INDEX order_items_order_id_idx   ON order_items (order_id);
CREATE INDEX order_items_product_id_idx ON order_items (product_id);
CREATE INDEX orders_customer_id_idx     ON orders (customer_id);

-- Set hint bits + visibility map (needed for index-only scans) and gather
-- fresh statistics. Must run outside a transaction block.
VACUUM (ANALYZE) customers, products, orders, order_items;

-- The target query filters  status = 'COMPLETED' AND order_date >= '2026-01-01'

-- join (and FK checks / deletes on orders). product_id likewise for products.
CREATE INDEX order_items_order_id_idx   ON order_items (order_id);
CREATE INDEX order_items_product_id_idx ON order_items (product_id);
CREATE INDEX orders_customer_id_idx     ON orders (customer_id);

-- Set hint bits + visibility map (needed for index-only scans) and gather
-- fresh statistics. Must run outside a transaction block.
VACUUM (ANALYZE) customers, products, orders, order_items;

   - **Main one:** `orders (status, order_date) INCLUDE (order_id)`. The filter matches about 28% of orders (half are COMPLETED, and about 9 of the 16 months fall on or after 2026-01-01). That's too many rows for an ordinary index on `(status, order_date)` to beat a full table scan. Adding `order_id`, the only other `orders` column the query needs, lets Postgres answer entirely from the index without reading the table.

`order_items` is still read with a full table scan. That's expected, because the query needs about 28% of its rows.
